questions.q: What must exist before any dbt model can ref() through source(), according to this lesson?
options: A sources.yml declaring the raw tables, with a freshness check on at least one
A generated dbt Docs site
A completed marts layer
Nothing — source() works automatically with no declaration
questions.explain: sources.yml declares the raw tables dbt is allowed to reference, one entry per raw table, and this lesson requires a freshness check on at least one.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a staging model contain?
options: A thin, one-to-one, typed wrapper over one raw table, with nothing joined in yet
Every raw source combined into one giant model
The final joined fact table, ready for BI tools
Only aggregated totals with no row-level detail
questions.explain: Staging models are 1:1 with a single raw source — typed and cleaned, but not yet joined to anything else.

questions.q: Where does the JSON source's flattening logic live in this capstone's dbt project?
options: In a one-off SQL script run before dbt, exactly as it was in the Snowflake capstone
It happens automatically with no code required
It cannot be done inside a dbt model at all
Inside the stg_events staging model itself, so dbt owns that transformation step
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly moves the flattening from a one-off script into the stg_events model, so dbt owns the transformation.

questions.q: What distinguishes int_orders_enriched from a marts-layer model, according to this lesson?
options: It has no surrogate keys yet and nothing outside the project queries it directly — it exists to make marts simpler
There is no meaningful difference between intermediate and marts models
It is materialized as a view while marts models never are
It contains no SQL at all
questions.explain: Intermediate models combine staging models but aren't endpoints themselves — that's what makes them intermediate rather than marts.

questions.q: Which models are allowed to query source() directly in this project's convention?
options: Only staging models — every other model downstream should use ref() instead
Only intermediate models
Only the marts layer
Every model in the project, at every layer
questions.explain: The lesson states staging models are the only layer that should query source() directly; everything downstream uses ref().
